cards.title: Introduction to Vue Reactivity
cards.content:
Reactivity is one of the core features of Vue.js. It allows your UI to automatically update when the underlying data changes, without manual DOM manipulation.

Vue 3 achieves this using JavaScript Proxies, wrapping your state objects to track dependencies and trigger updates.

cards.title: Ref vs Reactive
cards.content:
Vue provides two primary ways to create reactive state:

  • ref(): Takes an inner value and returns a reactive and mutable ref object. It can hold any value type, including primitives. Access the value via .value in script.
  • reactive(): Makes an entire object reactive. Works only with objects and arrays, not primitives. No .value needed.
import { ref, reactive } from 'vue';

const count = ref(0);
const state = reactive({ name: 'Vue', version: 3 });

count.value++;
state.version = 4;

options.text: reactive() is used for primitive values like strings and numbers.
ref() is used for primitive values and wraps them in an object with a .value property.
reactive() does not require importing from 'vue'.
ref() can only be used inside templates.

cards.title: Computed Properties
cards.content:
In-template expressions are convenient, but they should be kept simple. For complex logic that depends on reactive state, use computed properties.

Computed properties are cached based on their reactive dependencies and only re-evaluate when those dependencies change.

import { ref, computed } from 'vue';

const firstName = ref('John');
const lastName = ref('Doe');

const fullName = computed(() => `${firstName.value} ${lastName.value}`);

content.text: To create a calculated value that caches its result based on reactive dependencies, we use the [blank] function imported from 'vue'.

cards.title: Watchers and WatchEffects
cards.content:
Sometimes we need to perform side effects in reaction to state changes—such as mutating the DOM, fetching data, or logging analytics.

  • watch(): Lazily tracks specific reactive sources and runs a callback when they change.
  • watchEffect(): Runs the callback immediately while automatically tracking any reactive dependencies accessed synchronously.
import { ref, watch } from 'vue';

const question = ref('');

watch(question, async (newVal, oldVal) => {
  console.log(`Question changed from ${oldVal} to ${newVal}`);
});
